justice: The entire paved width is dedicated exclusively to motor vehicle lanes, demonstrating highly inequitable spatial distribution that marginalizes non-drivers.
The complete absence of sidewalks or curb ramps makes the environment entirely inaccessible for persons with disabilities, such as wheelchair users, and older adults.
Continuous metal guardrails along the edges create hard physical barriers, failing to provide a fair and inclusive environment for pedestrians or cyclists.
safety: The presence of a large commercial truck operating at likely high speeds next to a narrow shoulder creates a severe collision hazard for any unprotected road user.
The total lack of separated pedestrian or bicycle infrastructure leaves vulnerable groups (such as adolescents and the elderly) completely exposed to vehicular traffic.
While metal guardrails protect drivers from off-road hazards, they trap any potential pedestrians or cyclists on the shoulder with no safe escape route.
livability: The complete absence of residential buildings, commercial units, or community facilities indicates this space serves solely as a transit corridor rather than a livable environment.
There is no infrastructure to support social interaction or resting, such as benches or plazas, failing to meet the social needs of adolescents or older adults.
The hostile, car-dominated environment actively deters any form of pedestrian activity or community vitality.
sustainability: The extensive, wide asphalt paving maximizes impermeable surfaces, offering poor stormwater management and contributing to urban heat.
The complete lack of bicycle lanes and visible public transit infrastructure fails to support or encourage low-carbon, active travel modes.
However, the dense planting of mature trees and shrubs behind the right-side guardrail provides some ecological value through carbon sequestration and filtering.
aesthetics: The landscape is heavily dominated by monotonous gray asphalt and industrial metal guardrails, resulting in a sterile and uninviting visual environment.
Overhead power lines and tall, utilitarian street lighting poles clutter the sky view and detract from the overall visual harmony of the corridor.
The continuous rows of trees and vegetation on the right side provide a necessary visual break and introduce natural elements into the harsh infrastructure.
comfort: The lack of any pedestrian pathways, seating, or resting areas results in zero physical comfort for elderly or disabled users who might need to traverse the area.
The complete absence of shade structures or tree canopy over the roadway exposes any non-motorized user to direct sunlight, severely reducing thermal comfort.
The proximity to high-speed traffic lanes guarantees high noise levels and immense psychological stress (fear of collision) for any vulnerable road user.
walkability: There are absolutely no sidewalks or paved pedestrian pathways, forcing anyone on foot to walk on a dangerous, narrow vehicular shoulder.
Continuous metal guardrails block any potential pedestrian access to the adjacent planted verges or safer off-road areas.
The lack of crosswalks or pedestrian signals means there is no safe or defined way for pedestrians of any age or ability to cross the roadway.
bikeability: The absence of dedicated or protected bike lanes forces cyclists to share a narrow shoulder with high-speed motor vehicles and heavy trucks.
The solid white lane marking provides minimal visual separation from traffic, offering no actual physical protection or safety for cyclists.
The overall road design, optimized for high-speed vehicular throughput, creates a highly intimidating environment that completely discourages cycling for all social groups.
